metadata.title: Spectral Analysis of Systematic Residuals in Casimir Force Measurements: Lossless Vector Re-Audit, Statistical Pitfalls, and KPFM Patch-Potential Metrology (v2.0)
metadata.description: Revised Version 2.0. We establish a rigorous spectral metrology protocol for auditing Casimir force and pressure residuals and apply it to: (1) lossless vector-extracted measurements from the Au-Cu micro-electro-mechanical torsional oscillator (MTO, R = 294.3 um) experiment of Decca et al. (Phys. Rev. Lett. 91, 050402, 2003; N = 497 dynamic pressure residuals dPc and N = 288 static force residuals dFc), and (2) raw Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy (KPFM) and superconducting Casimir data from de Jong et al. (Nature Physics, 2025). We identify and resolve three metrological pitfalls: (i) applying an outlier-clipped Gaussian 3-sigma threshold to exponentially distributed (chi2_2/2) FFT periodograms flags 36 false peaks on white noise, while feeding Zechmeister-Kurster power into Scargle's unscaled exponential formula causes numerical underflow (FAP = 1.00); (ii) cubic polynomial detrending across short-range inverse-power tails (z < 400 nm) induces Runge oscillatory ringing (lambda = 583.5 nm, chi2/dof = 3.74, Baluev FAP = 1.5e-45), resolved via a physical {1, z^-4, z^-5} basis (chi2/dof = 1.14, P_max = 0.0332, Baluev FAP = 0.163) or linear-response window z >= 500 nm (chi2/dof = 1.20, Baluev FAP = 0.651); and (iii) uniform-grid spline resampling degrades short-wavelength 90% Minimum Detectable Levels by 1.9x-2.3x compared to the heteroscedastic Generalized Lomb-Scargle periodogram. Finally, Speake-Trenner Laplace integration of the 2D KPFM patch spectrum (V_rms = 42.42 mV, roughness = 2.22 nm) demonstrates from first principles that surface patch potentials produce a smooth monotonic drift (P_patch ~ d^-2.29) rather than periodic oscillations.
